key_insight: KaCGM parameterizes each causal structural equation with a Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN), yielding a generative causal model for mixed-type tabular data that is both expressive and directly inspectable for auditing.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of auditability in deep causal generative models for mixed-type tabular data by providing a structured, decomposable parameterization of structural equations that supports observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries.
method: Represent each structural equation in a causal graph using a Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN), exploiting a decomposition into simpler univariate components for interpretability.
Train a single generative causal model (KaCGM) on mixed-type tabular data to answer observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries while preserving component-wise inspectability.
Use the decomposition to expose per-variable functional contributions, enabling direct auditing and explanation of causal mechanisms without opaque black-box layers.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical, audit-friendly causal generative model for mixed-type tabular settings, improving explainability and trust when answering interventions and counterfactuals in high-stakes applications.
visual_elements: Causal graph diagram where each node's structural equation is annotated with a small KAN block to show modularity and per-variable inspectability.
Function-decomposition schematic illustrating the Kolmogorov–Arnold breakup: a multivariate mapping represented as a sum/composition of univariate components (KAN internals).
Before/after intervention panels: observed data distribution vs. interventional/counterfactual samples produced by KaCGM to demonstrate query types.
Audit dashboard mockup showing per-component plots and numeric summaries for a selected structural equation to highlight interpretability.
paper_authors: Alejandro Almodóvar, Mar Elizo, Patricia A. Apellániz, Santiago Zazo, Juan Parras
